author: simulation_agent

inequalities.inequality: save_interval << persistence time: resolve the ballistic lags and the crossover
fit lower bound >> persistence time: read the plateau and not D_T
max_lag_time >= a span above the lower bound: lags to fit

numbers.name: persistence_time_expected
numbers.note: 1/((d-1)*D_R) is 1/D_R in two dimensions. Consistent with the rotational diffusivity above BY CONSTRUCTION, which revision 2 was not: it carried the sweep top for one and the sweep bottom for the other, and A1 failed check 17 on the mismatch

numbers.name: lag_coverage_factor
numbers.note: save interval as a fraction of the persistence time: two decades of ballistic lag below the crossover

numbers.name: save_interval_max
numbers.note: upper bound. The crossover and the short-time slope live below tau_p, and a save interval near tau_p would record only the diffusive tail

numbers.name: plateau_factor
numbers.note: how many persistence times into the lag the effective diffusivity is read; the same input A2 derives its reference lag from, not A2's output (4.5.3 rule b)

numbers.name: fit_lag_range_lower_bound_min
numbers.note: the window parameter of effective_translational_diffusivity; a value read earlier is D_T under that name (contracts/observables.json)

numbers.name: window_span_factor
numbers.note: how many times the lower bound the MSD window extends, so the fit has lags to fit

numbers.name: max_lag_time_min
numbers.note: the window parameter of mean_squared_displacement, bounded from BELOW here: opposite to tracer_diffusivity, whose window is bounded from above to stay free

assumptions.statement: Two decades of lag below the persistence time is what it takes to see the ballistic slope of two, the crossover, and the approach to one on one curve; fewer would fit a slope through a crossover nobody resolved.
assumptions.falsifier: an msd_loglog_slope that reads two over the whole first decade retires the second

assumptions.statement: Ten persistence times is where the free active MSD is within a few per cent of its asymptotic slope. Interactions can lengthen the approach, which is a result.
assumptions.falsifier: a fitted slope that still drifts between ten and thirty persistence times raises this factor

assumptions.statement: A fit over lags from ten to thirty persistence times spans half a decade, enough for a weighted slope and short enough that the longest lag stays inside A2's record ratio.
assumptions.falsifier: a slope that changes with the upper end of the fit by more than the statistical error widens the span

note: Three windows, one per registered observable that this plan reads: the save interval for msd_loglog_slope and the crossover, the lower bound for effective_translational_diffusivity, and the span for mean_squared_displacement. A4 says nothing about the integration step.
